title: Social acceptability of face-worn cameras
bottleneck: Beyond technical privacy, wearing an obvious camera on your face in social settings triggers discomfort and confrontation: the 'glasshole' problem never went away. Subtle designs help but raise deception concerns; obvious designs invite stigma. Cultural norms around being recorded haven't adapted to face-worn sensors.
why_it_blocks: Social rejection can kill a product category faster than any technical flaw; AR glasses must be welcome in public to succeed. The industry hasn't solved the human side of the camera.
current_state: Display-less AI glasses are testing social waters with indicator lights and familiar sunglass designs. Public comfort with face cameras remains fragile and incident-prone. Each public confrontation over face cameras hardens norms against them, regardless of how useful the underlying AR becomes.
